title: Compact quasi-coherent derived objects on algebraic spaces are perfect
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover, and the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Use its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Perfect means etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $P\in C_X$ be compact [def-pc-compact-object]: for every small family $(L_\alpha)$ in $C_X$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(P,L_\alpha)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(P,\bigoplus_\alpha L_\alpha)$ is bijective. Then $P$ is perfect. This asserts compactness only in $C_X$, with no compactness hypothesis in all of $D(\mathcal O_X)$.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale chart $j:U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Since $X$ is quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-affine-source-qc-separated] makes $j$ quasi-compact and separated. Its diagonal is therefore quasi-compact: over an affine scheme test a closed immersion is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, with affine source. Thus $j$ is quasi-separated. By [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], $j^*=Lj^*$ is exact restriction, preserves quasi-coherent cohomology and is left adjoint to $Rj_*$. By [lem-sfb-space-derived-pushforward-coproducts], the latter preserves quasi-coherent cohomology and small coproducts. Thus this adjunction restricts to $C_U\rightleftarrows C_X$, with coproducts equal to the ambient derived coproducts.

source.place: Tag 09M8, proposition-compact-is-perfect, converse; affine reduction as in perfect.tex Tag 09M1, proposition-compact-is-perfect, final paragraph.

proof.text: Put $K=j^*P$. For any small family $(L_i)$ in $C_U$, the preceding adjunction and coproduct comparison give $\operatorname{Hom}_{C_U}(K,\bigoplus_i L_i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(P,\bigoplus_iRj_*L_i)\cong\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(P,Rj_*L_i)\cong\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_{C_U}(K,L_i)$. The middle bijection is the assumed compactness of $P$ [def-pc-compact-object]. Naturality of adjunction identifies these bijections with the map induced by the coproduct injections, so $K$ is compact in $C_U$.

source.place: Tag 09M8, proposition-compact-is-perfect, converse; affine reduction as in perfect.tex Tag 09M1, proposition-compact-is-perfect, final paragraph.

proof.text: Use the equivalence $a_A:D(A)\simeq C_U$ of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] and choose $E$ with $a_A(E)\cong K$. An equivalence preserves coproducts by their universal property: applying its fully faithful Hom bijections and essential surjectivity to the universal cocone gives the same universal cocone in the other category. Consequently, for every small family $(M_i)$ in $D(A)$, $\operatorname{Hom}(E,\bigoplus_iM_i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,\bigoplus_i a_A(M_i))\cong\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(E,M_i)$. These maps respect the injections; hence $E$ is compact [def-pc-compact-object].

source.place: Tag 09M8, proposition-compact-is-perfect, converse; affine reduction as in perfect.tex Tag 09M1, proposition-compact-is-perfect, final paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ring-derived-compact-perfect] to $E$, obtaining a bounded complex $F^\bullet$ whose terms split off finite free $A$-modules and with $F^\bullet\cong E$. The functor $a_A$ in [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] acts termwise. Its affine-etale formula $a_A(M)(\operatorname{Spec}B)=B\otimes_A M$ identifies $a_A(A^n)$ with $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$. Applying it to $p_ri_r=1$ gives the same splitting for $a_A(F^r)$. Thus $a_A(F^\bullet)$ is strictly perfect and isomorphic to $K$ in the derived category; the boundedness interval is unchanged.

source.place: Tag 09M8, proposition-compact-is-perfect, converse; affine reduction as in perfect.tex Tag 09M1, proposition-compact-is-perfect, final paragraph.

proof.text: Represent $P$ by a complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the small etale site and choose a K-injective resolution of it, a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex $I$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; then $I$ also represents $P$. Its restriction $I|_U$ to $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U$, the etale site of $U$, is K-injective [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] and represents $K=j^*P$, because etale pullback is exact restriction [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. Apply [lem-pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local] on the ringed site $(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_U)$ at its final object $U$, with $\mathcal L^\bullet=a_A(F^\bullet)$ and the K-injective complex $I|_U$: the derived isomorphism $a_A(F^\bullet)\cong K$ of step 4 equals $Q_U(f)$ for a chain map $f:a_A(F^\bullet)\to I|_U$. Since the cohomology sheaf functors factor through the derived category, $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Now let $V\to X$ be any object of the small etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space] and put $W=V\times_XU$; it is a scheme etale over $V$ because $j$ is representable and etale, and $\{W\to V\}$ is a covering because $j$ is surjective. Restrict $f$ along $W\to U$ (relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]): this gives a chain map $a_A(F^\bullet)|_W\to I|_W$, again a quasi-isomorphism because restriction is exact [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. Its source vanishes outside the bounds of $F^\bullet$, and restricting the maps $a_A(i_r),a_A(p_r)$ of step 4 exhibits each term as a direct summand of $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n_r}$. This is exactly the local condition of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] for the representative $I$ at $V$, with the one-member covering $\{W\to V\}$. Therefore $P$ is perfect.
